subtitulo: Always, never, really — in the right place
descripcion: English adverbs of frequency and manner have fixed positions that don't match a direct translation from Spanish. At B2 the goal is to place always, never, usually and similar adverbs correctly before the main verb but after be, and to know where manner adverbs go at the end of a clause.

filas: before the main verb, after be
She always arrives on time. / She is always on time.

ejemplos.texto: She always arrives exactly on time.
He explained it slowly and clearly.
It's really important to check this first.

notas: With be, the frequency adverb comes after it: she is never late, not she never is late.
With auxiliary verbs (have, will, can), the adverb goes between the auxiliary and the main verb: she has always liked it.
Manner adverbs at the start of a sentence are possible for emphasis but sound more literary: slowly, she opened the door.

es.en: Spanish places frequency adverbs more freely, often at the start or end of the sentence («siempre llega a tiempo»). Spanish speakers tend to put always and never at the start of the English sentence, where it sounds marked or wrong.
es.es: El español coloca los adverbios de frecuencia con mayor libertad, a menudo al principio o al final («siempre llega a tiempo»). Los hispanohablantes tienden a poner «always» y «never» al principio de la oración inglesa, donde suenan marcados o incorrectos.

de.en: German places frequency adverbs after the verb («Er kommt immer pünktlich»), which produces He comes always on time. English places always, never and usually before the main verb (He always comes on time), but after be (He is always late).
de.de: Im Deutschen stehen Häufigkeitsadverbien nach dem Verb («Er kommt immer pünktlich»), wodurch «He comes always on time» entsteht. Im Englischen stehen «always», «never» und «usually» vor dem Vollverb («He always comes on time»), aber nach «be» («He is always late»).

it.en: Italian places frequency and manner adverbs after the verb («arriva sempre in orario; parlo bene l'inglese»), which leads to He arrives always on time and I speak well English. English places always before the main verb and keeps the object next to the verb (I speak English well).
it.it: L'italiano colloca gli avverbi di frequenza e maniera dopo il verbo («arriva sempre in orario»; «parlo bene l'inglese»), il che porta a «He arrives always on time» e «I speak well English». L'inglese mette «always» prima del verbo principale e mantiene l'oggetto vicino al verbo («I speak English well»).

fr.en: French places frequency and manner adverbs after the verb («il arrive toujours à l'heure; je parle bien anglais»), which leads to He arrives always on time and I speak well English. English places always before the main verb and keeps the object next to the verb.
fr.fr: Le français place les adverbes de fréquence et de manière après le verbe («il arrive toujours à l'heure» ; «je parle bien anglais»), ce qui conduit à «He arrives always on time» et «I speak well English». L'anglais place «always» avant le verbe principal et garde l'objet près du verbe.

pt.en: Brazilian Portuguese usually places «sempre» before the verb («ele sempre chega na hora»), which matches English (He always arrives on time). European Portuguese places it after the verb («ele chega sempre a horas»), which leads to He arrives always on time.
pt.pt: No português brasileiro, «sempre» costuma vir antes do verbo («ele sempre chega na hora»), como em inglês («He always arrives on time»). No português europeu, vem depois («ele chega sempre a horas»), o que pode levar a «He arrives always on time».

errores: Placing a frequency adverb at the start or end of the sentence instead of before the main verb.
Putting the frequency adverb before be instead of after it.
Placing a manner adverb between the verb and its object: he explained slowly the plan instead of he explained the plan slowly.

es: «*ya no*» rendered as *already not*: *I already don't live there* instead of *I no longer live there*.
de: Keeping the German order time–manner–place: *I travel today by train to Bern* instead of *I'm travelling to Bern by train today*.
it: «*non … più*» rendered as *not … more*: *I don't live there more* instead of *I don't live there any more*.
fr: «*ne … plus*» rendered as *not … more*: *I don't smoke more* instead of *I don't smoke any more*.
pt: «*já não*» rendered as *already not*: *I already don't work there* instead of *I no longer work there*.

redemittel.funcion: sentence adverb at the end, informal

redemittel.expresion: Before the verb or after it?

mision.consigna: Describe your news habits for a survey on how people follow the news.
requisitos: six frequency adverbs in the right place
two with *be* and two with auxiliaries
one adverb at the end of the sentence
use *headline*, *to form an opinion* and *freedom of the press*

microtareas.texto: Five sentences about the news with *always*, *usually*, *never*.
Check: before the main verb, after *be*?
Record 90 seconds: how do you *fact-check* a *headline*?

autochequeo: Is the frequency adverb placed before the main verb, or after be?
Is the manner adverb at the end, not between the verb and its object?
Have I avoided putting always or never at the very start of the sentence?
Does the position sound natural, not translated from Spanish?
Are at least four different adverb positions used correctly?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on adverb placement. Check the position of frequency adverbs relative to be and main verbs, and the position of manner adverbs relative to the object. Do not rewrite the text.
